intro: とき is a noun meaning "time", so it attaches exactly as any noun does when a clause modifies it: 行くとき, 寒いとき, 暇なとき, 子供のとき. The clause before とき names a moment or period, and the main clause says what happens at that time. The one thing English speakers must learn is that the tense before とき is relative to the main verb, not to now.

skills.rule: [plain verb / i-adjective / na-adjective + な / noun + の] とき: "at the time when"; dictionary form = not yet happened at that point, た form = already happened.
skills.explain:
Attach とき like a noun: verbs and i-adjectives in plain form (読むとき, 読んだとき, 読まないとき, 寒いとき), na-adjectives with な (暇なとき), nouns with の (子供のとき, 雨のとき).

The tense before とき is measured from the main event. 日本に行くとき、カメラを買った: the going had not happened yet, so the camera was bought before or on the way. 日本に行ったとき、カメラを買った: the going was complete, so the camera was bought in Japan. The same holds for the future: 日本に行ったとき、買います (I'll buy it once I'm there).

とき alone, ときに and ときは are all correct. ときに pins a single event to that moment (出るときに鍵をかけた). ときは sets a general frame, often before advice or a habit (困ったときは電話して). とき itself only states time: for a hypothetical "if" (もし…たら) or "once X, then" use たら, and for a span during which something else happens use 間.

examples.jp: 子供[こども]の{とき}、よく川[かわ]で泳[およ]ぎました。
examples.en: When I was a child, I often swam in the river.

examples.jp: 暇[ひま]な{とき}、何[なに]をしますか。
examples.en: What do you do when you're free?

examples.jp: 寝[ね]る{とき}、電気[でんき]を消[け]します。
examples.en: I turn off the light when I go to bed.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]へ行[い]った{とき}、昔[むかし]の友達[ともだち]に会[あ]いました。
examples.en: When I went to Japan, I met an old friend there.

examples.jp: 家[いえ]を出[で]る{ときに}、鍵[かぎ]をかけるのを忘[わす]れた。
examples.en: I forgot to lock the door when I was leaving the house.

examples.jp: 困[こま]った{ときは}、いつでも連絡[れんらく]してください。
examples.en: If you ever run into trouble, contact me any time.

contrast.note: たら is a condition or "once X happens, then": 駅に着いたら電話して (call me once you arrive). とき only marks the time of an occasion that comes round; it cannot carry a one-off hypothesis (もし宝くじに当たったら) or a discovery (家に帰ったら手紙が来ていた).
まえに is strictly "before": 寝る前に歯を磨く. 寝るとき is "at bedtime", the moment of going to bed, not the period before it.
間 / 間に marks a stretch of time during which something else happens, often with a different subject: 母が寝ている間に掃除した. とき picks out a point or occasion.

mistakes.bad: 子供[こども]{とき}、犬[いぬ]が怖[こわ]かった。
mistakes.good: 子供[こども]の{とき}、犬[いぬ]が怖[こわ]かった。
mistakes.note: A noun needs の before とき.

mistakes.bad: 暇[ひま]{とき}、本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。
mistakes.good: 暇[ひま]な{とき}、本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。
mistakes.note: A na-adjective needs な before とき.

mistakes.bad: 日本[にほん]に着[つ]く{とき}、空港[くうこう]で両替[りょうがえ]しました。
mistakes.good: 日本[にほん]に着[つ]いた{とき}、空港[くうこう]で両替[りょうがえ]しました。
mistakes.note: You changed money after landing, so the arrival is complete: た form before とき.

skills.tip: Ask: had the とき event already finished when the main thing happened? Yes: た form. Not yet: dictionary form.
